hints: Use $A/(3x+2)+(Bx+C)/(x^2+5)$ because the quadratic factor is irreducible.
Clear denominators, set $x=-2/3$ to determine $A$, and compare the remaining coefficients to find $B$ and $C$.
walkthrough:
State the partial fraction decomposition for a linear factor and an irreducible quadratic factor:
$$\dfrac{5x^2 - 7x + 4}{(3x + 2)(x^2 + 5)} = \dfrac{A}{3x + 2} + \dfrac{Bx + C}{x^2 + 5}$$

Clear fractions by multiplying both sides by $(3x + 2)(x^2 + 5)$:
$$5x^2 - 7x + 4 = A(x^2 + 5) + (Bx + C)(3x + 2)$$

Determine the constant $A$ by substituting the root of the linear factor, $x = -\dfrac{2}{3}$:
$$\text{LHS} = 5\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 - 7\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right) + 4 = 5\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right) + \dfrac{14}{3} + 4 = \dfrac{20}{9} + \dfrac{42}{9} + \dfrac{36}{9} = \dfrac{98}{9}$$
$$\text{RHS} = A\left(\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 + 5\right) = A\left(\dfrac{4}{9} + \dfrac{45}{9}\right) = \dfrac{49}{9}A$$
Equating LHS and RHS: $\dfrac{49}{9}A = \dfrac{98}{9} \implies A = 2$.

Determine the constant $C$ by substituting $x = 0$:
$$4 = A(5) + C(2) = 2(5) + 2C = 10 + 2C$$
$$2C = 4 - 10 = -6 \implies C = -3$$

Determine the constant $B$ by equating coefficients of $x^2$ on both sides:
$$5 = A + 3B = 2 + 3B$$
$$3B = 5 - 2 = 3 \implies B = 1$$

State the complete partial fractions form:
$$f(x) = \dfrac{2}{3x + 2} + \dfrac{x - 3}{x^2 + 5}$$

hints: Expand the two partial fractions from part (i) separately through $x^2$.
Multiply the second series by $x-3$, discard powers above $x^2$, and combine like terms.
walkthrough:
Expand the first partial fraction $\dfrac{2}{3x + 2}$ using the binomial series for $(1 + u)^{-1} = 1 - u + u^2 - \cdots$:
$$\dfrac{2}{3x + 2} = 2(2 + 3x)^{-1} = 2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^{-1} = \left(1 + \dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^{-1}$$
$$= 1 - \left(\dfrac{3}{2}x\right) + \left(\dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^2 - \cdots = 1 - \dfrac{3}{2}x + \dfrac{9}{4}x^2 - \cdots$$

Expand the denominator factor of the second partial fraction $(x^2 + 5)^{-1}$:
$$(5 + x^2)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{5}\left(1 + \dfrac{x^2}{5}\right)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{5}\left(1 - \dfrac{x^2}{5} + \cdots\right) = \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{25}x^2 + \cdots$$

Multiply by the numerator $(x - 3)$ and retain terms up to $x^2$:
$$\dfrac{x - 3}{x^2 + 5} = (x - 3)\left(\dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{25}x^2 + \cdots\right)$$
$$= -3\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right) + x\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right) - 3\left(-\dfrac{1}{25}x^2\right) + \cdots = -\dfrac{3}{5} + \dfrac{1}{5}x + \dfrac{3}{25}x^2 + \cdots$$

Sum both expansions to find $f(x)$ up to the $x^2$ term:
$$f(x) = \left(1 - \dfrac{3}{2}x + \dfrac{9}{4}x^2\right) + \left(-\dfrac{3}{5} + \dfrac{1}{5}x + \dfrac{3}{25}x^2\right)$$

Calculate the coefficients by collecting like terms:
$$\text{Constant term}: 1 - \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{2}{5}$$
$$\text{Coefficient of } x: -\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{-15 + 2}{10} = -\dfrac{13}{10}$$
$$\text{Coefficient of } x^2: \dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{3}{25} = \dfrac{225 + 12}{100} = \dfrac{237}{100}$$
